name: terraform-mlops-delivery-module-refactor
instr:
The Terraform for our MLOps production model-delivery stack in `/workspace/infra` has grown into one flat root module: everything is declared at the top level, the per-model resources are `count`-indexed by list position, and names, settings and tags are hard-coded all over the files. Split it into three local modules (registry, serving and pipeline) without touching the running infrastructure: against the current state, the plan has to come out as nothing but moves.

For the no-pasted-identifiers rule below, a "part" of an existing ID, ARN, IP address or DNS name means an opaque, cloud-assigned component extracted from state or plan data. It does not mean a user-configured component of a resource name that is already written in the legacy `.tf` files, even though providers also include that configured name in an ID, ARN or DNS name. Keep every such configured component at today's value unless a variable or key requirement below explicitly says it controls that component; do not regenerate or derive it from other inputs.

There is no AWS access from this machine. `terraform init` works offline from the local provider mirror, `terraform.tfstate` is a copy of the production state, and `scripts/ci-plan.sh` runs what CI runs: a `terraform plan -refresh=false` against the state followed by the guardrail policies in `policies/`.

## Detailed Constraints

**How CI judges the change.** CI takes the repository alone and plans it with `terraform plan -refresh=false` against its own cop
